$comment: The vocabulary of example tags (examples/README.md, Find an example). An example's tags in example.json must come from here; build.py refuses others. Add a tag only when no existing one fits, with a description that says when an agent should reach for it.

domain.payments: Money and orders: holds, payments, refunds, prices and discounts (the Box Office ticketing system)
domain.messaging: Kafka and message handling: codecs, partitioning, listeners, batch commits, what a consumer does with a message
domain.consensus: Agreement among replicas: Raft, quorums, majorities, terms
domain.leader-election: Raft leader election: terms, votes, the role machine, timeouts, stepping down
domain.log-replication: Raft log replication: append entries, the consistency check, commit index, a leader's record of its followers
domain.quorums: Majority and quorum arithmetic, and counting replicas or votes
domain.distributed-transactions: Two-phase commit: coordinators, participants, votes, decisions, timeouts, crash recovery
domain.replicated-data: Data replicated without consensus: hybrid logical clocks, last-writer-wins resolution
domain.clocks-and-time: Clocks, timestamps, skew, deadlines, expiry, anything that reads the time
domain.resilience: Retries, backoff, circuit breakers and rate limiters: what a service does when a dependency misbehaves
domain.idempotency: Idempotency keys and at-most-once execution of retried requests
domain.transactions: Local transaction boundaries: when a framework commits or rolls back
domain.authentication: Tokens and their validation: JWT timestamps, signatures, skew
domain.access-control: Who may access what: visibility and access rules
domain.deserialization: Turning bytes into objects, and what a payload can make the code do
domain.jvm-internals: The JVM's own rules (JVMS): class files, the verifier, the interpreter, class initialization, linking
domain.class-files: Class file structures: the constant pool, attributes, exception tables, stack map frames, encodings in them
domain.bytecode-verification: The type checker and the stack and frame computations a verifier relies on
domain.class-initialization: Class initialization and loading under threads (JVMS 5.5)
domain.interpreter-semantics: What an instruction must do: integer division, float comparison, intrinsics
domain.compilers: Code generation decisions: switch lowering, lookupswitch tables, binary search over them
domain.text-encoding: Character encodings: modified UTF-8, hexadecimal, Unicode digits and surrogates
domain.numeric-code: Arithmetic-heavy methods: powers, divisions, bit tricks, table sizes, comparisons of numbers
domain.array-utilities: Methods over arrays and index ranges: reverse, subarray, search, sort, copying into a buffer
domain.open-source-libraries: A change to a published library, verified from its bytecode: the real-world examples
domain.spring-boot: Spring Boot services: controllers and their routes, beans under @Transactional and other proxied advice, listeners, schedules, bean validation, configuration keys; what the framework does around the code rather than in it

defect.integer-overflow: Arithmetic that wraps around: a sum, product, difference, absolute value or cast past the type's range
defect.off-by-one: A boundary one off: inclusive against exclusive ends, a count that includes itself, a length short by a header
defect.rounding: Integer division and rounding that drift or round the wrong way
defect.special-values: The values a rule treats specially: null, NaN, Integer.MIN_VALUE, division by zero
defect.dropped-case: A case lost in a rewrite: merged switch arms, one rule for several situations, a branch folded away
defect.nondeterminism: A result that depends on the clock, randomness or the thread, where it must be a function of the inputs
defect.hidden-capability: Code that gains a capability it should not have: reflection, class loading, the clock, threads, randomness
defect.security-boundary: A check that guards a security property: type safety, access rules, token validity, input filtering
defect.race-condition: Interleavings of concurrent actors that the code did not expect
defect.deadlock: A state from which nothing can move
defect.liveness: Something that should eventually happen never does: a decision, a probe, a refill, catching up
defect.agreement: Replicas or participants that end up disagreeing: two leaders, a split decision, divergent values
defect.lost-committed-data: Data that was committed, or acknowledged, and is later lost or overwritten
defect.stale-messages: Messages that arrive late, after the receiver has moved on to a newer term or state
defect.duplicate-delivery: Retries and messages that arrive twice, or a request executed twice
defect.crash-recovery: What a process does when it restarts, and what its log lets it know
defect.write-ahead-ordering: The order of logging and sending: a side effect before the record that should precede it
defect.exceptions: The exceptional path: what throws, when, and an exception claimed unreachable
defect.buffer-bounds: Reading or writing past what a buffer or array holds, or allocating absurd sizes
defect.composition: A bug between components each of whose contracts approves it: glue, assumptions about who runs first
defect.configuration-drift: A setting and the code that reads it no longer agree: a key mistyped or set under a prefix nothing binds, a key renamed in the code but not in application.yaml, a key the framework has deprecated, a value of the wrong type. Reach for it when the change is in a configuration file, a @ConfigurationProperties prefix or a @Value placeholder, and no test runs with the profile in question.
defect.validation-gap: A Bean Validation constraint that compiles and never runs: a nested type's constraints with no @Valid leading into them, a request body taken without @Valid, a constraint in a group the handler does not ask for, a constraint on a type its validator cannot handle (which fails at the first request instead). Reach for it when the change adds or moves a constraint and the tests send valid data.
defect.inert-annotation: An annotation nothing reads: the switch that registers its interceptor (@EnableCaching, @EnableAsync, @EnableScheduling, @EnableMethodSecurity, an auto-configuration whose condition holds, a Bean Validation provider) is missing, so the code compiles, the context starts, the tests pass, and the method is never cached, run, scheduled or secured. Reach for it when the change adds an advice annotation and nothing else, or drops a starter from the build.

technique.contract-diff-review: An intended change reviewed as the diff of a derived contract
technique.confined-change: A regression proof that the change affects only the inputs the developer declared (--unchanged-unless, intendedInputs)
technique.jml-quantifiers: A property over arrays with JML quantifiers: \forall, \exists, \sum, \num_of, \max, \min
technique.jml-old: A property that compares an array with its state at the call (\old): frame conditions, permutations
technique.throws-clause: A property with a throws clause, which brings the exceptional path under the proof
technique.tla-liveness: Liveness under fairness: something eventually happens, with a counterexample that goes on forever
technique.tla-refinement: A model checked to implement a more abstract specification
technique.tla-inductive-invariant: An invariant checked from every state it admits, proving safety by induction, with one-step counterexamples
technique.tla-action-property: A property of each step rather than each state ([][A]_v)
technique.tla-symmetry: A bigger configuration made affordable by a symmetry set
technique.tla-history-variables: Variables that record the whole run, so that claims about a run become invariants
technique.tla-coverage: What a verdict rests on: which contract rows a run takes, and vacuous verdicts
technique.tla-trace-validation: Recorded runs of the Java code checked step by step against the model
technique.tla-fault-configuration: A configuration that lets the environment misbehave: crashes and restarts, delayed or duplicated messages, expiry
technique.tla-unreachable-exception: An exception the kernel reserves for an impossible input, proved unreachable in every run
technique.generated-operator: A TLA+ operator generated from a Java method's contract, so the model runs the proven bytecode
technique.multiple-configurations: One model checked under several configurations, the verdict being the first that fails
technique.pull-request-review: A pull request or commit to a library verified from its compiled bytecode with /verify-bytecode
technique.jdk-models: JDK classes JBMC has no model of, and the models that fix the false violations they cause
technique.solver-limits: Where the prover gives no verdict or a wrong one: timeouts, memory, division, arrays of computed size
